ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EEAS), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance sanctions list; mandatory PEP identification and risk rating per FATF Recommendations 12 and 22 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, sanctions-designated persons, and high-risk third countries identified by FATF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be composed in French, German, or Luxembourgish (official languages of Luxembourg); the RCS operates primarily in French and requires the name to be written in Latin script; a name in any non-Latin script must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet. The name must be distinctive, lawful, not contrary to public order, and must include the legal form designation 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or its abbreviation 'SARL'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société d'investissement à capital fixe / variable
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the LBR/RCS rejects a proposed company name, the applicant may file a written re-examination request with the RCS within 15 days of the rejection notice. If the rejection is maintained, an administrative appeal may be brought before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber) within 40 days under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies; legal counsel representation is strongly recommended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally accepted for registered-office purposes in Luxembourg, provided the company maintains substantive presence in the Grand Duchy (management and administration functions, business records, and decision-making). For a wholesale distribution entity, the Luxembourg tax administration and the CSSF expect real economic substance; a mere mail-forwarding address creates risks of fiscal reclassification, permanent establishment characterization, and denial of treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a low-risk, non-regulated wholesale trading company: estimated probability below 5% per 12-month cycle, although the Luxembourg tax administration and the CSSF retain full statutory inspection and investigation powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; S.à r.l. governed by Articles 710-1 to 710-20; supplemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized or private articles of incorporation (statuts) together with the signed RCS declaration of incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation. For cash contributions, the full amount must be deposited with a Luxembourg bank and evidenced by a banker's certificate; the funds remain blocked until the entity obtains RCS registration. No separate statutory escrow account is required beyond this blocked deposit mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribing shareholders' allotment in the attached share subscription list is approved, and that each share be fully paid up in cash or in-kind in accordance with Article 710-1 of the 1915 Commercial Companies Law. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company shall be established at [registered address], Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that the manager shall file the appropriate rectification with the RCS upon any relocation. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed sole manager (Gérant) of the company with full legal, banking, and operational authority, and that he or she shall have full authority to execute all incorporation formalities. RESOLVED, that this resolution takes effect immediately upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open and fund the blocked capital deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Luxembourg credit institution providing the banker's certificate for RCS purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Luxembourg bank to open a blocked account in the name of the future company, deposit not less than EUR 12,000, and obtain a certificate confirming that the minimum capital is fully subscribed and that funds are available for release only after RCS registration. Provide source-of-funds documentation if requested by the bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the deposit, provide additional source-of-funds documents and obtain a corrected certificate before proceeding; if the certificate is deficient, request re-issuance by the bank before the notarial filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Notaire) or, where permitted, private deed authenticated in the form required by Luxembourg law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review and execute the statuts containing corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose covering wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames, share capital, share classes, management powers, and fiscal identification language. If the notary is used, the notary delivers the electronic filing instruction to LBR. The first manager must accept appointment before filing.
required_dossiers: Copy of registered office lease or domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendments, revise the draft and execute an amended instrument; for in-kind contributions, obtain a statutory auditors' valuation certificate and explain any material discrepancies to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation documents with the RCS and obtain legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing portal for the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized or private deed of incorporation, the bank certificate, the manager's acceptance, and the RCS electronic declaration through LBR. Pay the prescribed registration fee. Upon validation, the RCS assigns the Luxembourg entity number and the company acquires legal personality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS files a query, cure the stated formal deficiency within the prescribed time through the LBR portal and resubmit the corrected document; if the application is refused, submit a written request for reconsideration with corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Luxembourg tax and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via the MyGuichet online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the commencement notice with the ACD, request a Luxembourg VAT number, and register for corporate income tax and municipal business tax where applicable. Provide the RCS extract and tax representative details if required. VAT registration is mandatory before invoicing intra-EU sales.
required_dossiers: RCS extract of the articles of incorporation
Manager identity and Luxembourg residence status
Proof of business activity under ISIC 4646
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Reply to the ACD notice through MyGuichet with any missing documents; if VAT registration is delayed, file with the competent registration office and request expedited processing on the basis of the completed RCS dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Luxembourg social security institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the employer and manager registration form to the CCSS. The company will be assigned a social security numbers file to declare the manager-director and any employees. Pay any applicable civil servant contributions or affiliate contributions in accordance with the Luxembourg Social Security Code.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS query requires missing payroll details, amend the declaration online; for late registration, provide a written justification and request reassessment of any potential penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the official electronic gazette and commercial readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS official publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations; Ministry of the Economy for establishment authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the RCS legal publication has been effected after incorporation. If the company intends to conduct wholesale warehousing or distribution operations, apply for the establishment permit under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to regulated professions and ensure the registered office premises comply with occupational and fire safety requirements.
required_dossiers: Establishment permit application if commercial storage is active
Premises address and safety inspection records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication or authorization is delayed, contact LBR and the Ministry of Economy in writing; any ministerial silence remedy may be available under Luxembourg administrative law after the statutory decision deadline passes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des Classes moyennes et de l'entrepreneuriat
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the regulation of access to professions of craftsman, trader and industrialist

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Registration only / full EIA report not triggered for wholesale distribution and warehousing of ophthalmic eyeglass frames; not listed in the mandatory EIA classes under Annexes I and II of the implementing regulation, unless the warehouse exceeds applicable storage-volume thresholds, in which case a registration notification may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial production process is carried out; sanitary wastewater discharges to municipal sewerage must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 7 March 2007 on wastewater discharge. Storage of plastic frame materials and packaging must comply with the Luxembourg waste management Law of 21 March 2012 on waste, including household and non-hazardous commercial waste record-keeping. VOC thresholds of the EU 2004/42/EC Directive are not triggered absent coating or finishing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety declaration for business premises, if open to the public or comprising a warehouse, under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 3 November 2008 on fire safety; structural load certification for storage racking; occupational workplace risk assessment and ITM registration under Articles L.312-1 et seq. of the Luxembourg Labor Code.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange control administration. EU free movement of capital and payments (Articles 63-66 TFEU) applies, with bank supervision and AML/CFT enforcement by the CSSF under the amended Law of 12 November 2004.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both capital and current account. Luxembourg is part of the Eurosystem; the euro is fully convertible and no prior exchange-control authorization is required for profit remittance, dividend distribution, shareholder loan repayment, or capital repatriation by an ordinary wholesale SARL. Dividends and profit distributions are subject only to Luxembourg corporate formalities: ordinary general meeting approval, the Article 710-6 balance-sheet/solvency test of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, and CSSF AML/CFT payment screening. Foreign-currency receipts (USD, CNY) are freely depositable and convertible into EUR at the foreign-exchange desks of Luxembourg credit institutions without surrender obligation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory timeline for repatriation, liquidation, or conversion of export proceeds. An ISIC 4646 wholesale exporter is free to retain USD/CNY export receipts in multicurrency accounts for constructive matching of procurement payables. The only compliance obligation is the bank's periodic Balance-of-Payments statistical reporting to the BCL for cross-border transactions above applicable per-transaction thresholds; no mandatory conversion percentage applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with strict limits. Luxembourg-licensed payment institutions and e-money institutions under the Law of 1 August 2018 (implementing PSD2) can open EUR IBAN accounts and execute SEPA, SEPA Instant, and SWIFT cross-border payments for low-value open-account disbursements (supplier prepayments, platform payouts, refunds). However, an EMI is neither a credit institution nor a provider of documentary trade finance; it cannot issue standby letters of credit, activate MT700 documentary credits, or process principal trade settlement flows for ISIC 4646 volumes without a sponsoring Tier-1 bank. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK/US fintech platforms not passporting under the CSSF) have low viability for principal flows due to correspondent banking friction, no Luxembourg RBE nexus, and the CSSF's territorial prudential scope; the blueprint therefore reserves platform rails for ancillary disbursements only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory KYC applies to the SARL's authorized signatories, directors, shareholders holding at least 25%, and beneficial owners (UBO) under the amended Law of 12 November 2004. Tier-1 Luxembourg banks generally require at least one physical meeting with the primary executive director or UBO, either at a Luxembourg branch or at a CSSF-regulated foreign branch under a recognized group KYC arrangement. Remote/video identification is technically permitted where the bank's internal policy accepts CSSF-recognized video ID and is combined with notarized passport/ID copies, apostilled power of attorney, extracts from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), and UBO registration extracts from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) under the Law of 13 January 2019. For an entity with no Luxembourg premises or directors, the realistic onboarding route is the appointment of a Luxembourg-licensed professional director or a local registered office and a full compliance interview with the director(s) in Luxembourg; expected clearance: 4-10 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO or parent shareholder domiciled in a FATF high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg RBE extract, notarized beneficial ownership chain, RCS extract, sanctions screening certificates (UN/EU/OFAC), CRS/FATCA self-certifications, audited parent accounts for the last three years, evidence of the group's real economic activity (employee records, operating leases, distribution agreements), and a formal Luxembourg legal opinion confirming full transparency under the AML Law of 12 November 2004.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or sanctions-list hits on directors, counterparties, or target end-markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificates of good conduct from each country of residence, sworn declarations of the individuals, independent enhanced due diligence (EDD) report by a KYC/GRC provider, denied-party screening outputs covering the complete trading-counterparty and customer master list, and a market-review memorandum demonstrating the absence of sanctioned-entity nexus in the optical wholesale supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or non-documentable source of the initial €12,000 SARL share capital and subsequent shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blocked capital reception certificate issued by the beneficiary bank, notarial deed of incorporation, board resolution for the capital injection, 24-month bank statements of the transferring entity, audited financial statements and tax returns of the shareholder, signed share subscription agreements, and a source-of-wealth declaration corroborated by sale/acquisition agreements or inheritance documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected velocity or economic mismatch (large USD inbound settlements against EUR/CNY outbound payables) triggering a cash-intensive-spread profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury and FX risk policy approved by the board, three-year commercial pipeline with pro-forma invoices from eyewear frame OEMs, supplier framework contracts, ISDA Master Agreement strategy, a precise EMIR essential-hedging assessment showing no speculative positions, and an AML transactional-monitoring commitment letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency / 'letterbox company' risk raised during the KYC interview for a newly formed SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft employment or delegation agreements, local office lease, RCS physical address evidence, minutes of the board of managers establishing operational residence, distribution agreements with brand owners, insurance policies, and a multi-year substance trajectory plan acceptable to CSSF-supervised credit institutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire protocol: the parent/shareholder remits the subscription proceeds by SWIFT MT103 in EUR (or USD converted at the receiving bank) to the SARL's blocked capital account (compte de consignation/attestation) opened at the Tier-1 Luxembourg bank prior to notarial incorporation. The MT103 field 70 (Remittance Information) must state: 'Capital subscription – [SARL full name] – RCS number – shareholder identity'. The bank will apply the BCL Balance-of-Payments statistical classification for direct-investment equity and will release the block only upon the notary's attestation of receipt. The statutory minimum is €12,000 nominal capital, with at least 25% of each subscribed contribution paid up (€3,000 minimum in cash) at formation; after incorporation, additional injections are booked as capital increase or shareholder current-account loans and require a general meeting resolution and, for loans, a written advance agreement with arm's-length interest to prevent recharacterization as permanent equity. Funds from outside the EEA are further subject to standard correspondent-bank UBO verification, sanctions screening, and the CSSF's know-your-fund analysis; no exchange-control license is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Open-account settlements for ISIC 4646 frame purchases are executed by SWIFT MT103 (country-wide payment) from the SARL's EUR or USD operational account, with the remittance information containing the commercial invoice number, the LC reference where applicable, and the purpose classification for foreign trade (import of goods, i.e., BPM6 goods category). EU suppliers are paid by SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT or SCT Inst) using beneficiary IBAN. For contractually secured trade, the bank issues documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700 and acts as reimbursing bank under MT740; confirmations by Asian seller-side banks are arranged to mitigate country and availability risk. Typical LC documentation for ophthalmic frames: commercial invoice, full-set original bill of lading or house air waybill, packing list, and beneficiary certificate of origin. Platform_Pay rails, where adopted, are restricted to low-value disbursements (sales commissions, catalogue design payments, customs-broker fees) through a regulated Luxembourg payment institution and are reconciled invoice-by-invoice against the enterprise treasury ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) — vanilla deliverable forwards concluded under bilateral confirmations and, where applicable, an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement; permitted for hedging documented invoice and purchase-order exposures only.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — EUR/CNY and similar onshore-restricted pairs, permitted only through CSSF-licensed counterparts and subject to EMIR trade reporting and essential-hedging documentation.

Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) — permitted for treasury balance-sheet hedging of USD receivables against CNY payables; must be assessed against EMIR clearing thresholds and non-cleared margin rules (Article 11 EMIR) if the counterparty exceeds relevant thresholds.

FX Options and Zero-Cost Collar Structures (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) — permitted under a board-approved treasury mandate, treated as cash-flow hedges under IFRS 9 when matched against the expected wholesale sales and procurement pipeline, and subject to strict market-risk limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year end; for calendar-year entity, no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to EUR 1,000; written notice from RCS; persistent default may trigger administrative strike-off or dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the calendar month containing the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 500 to EUR 10,000 per sanction schedule; criminal liability for directors in case of repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers; no later than 6 months after year-end otherwise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; late-filing fines up to EUR 25,000; possible tax auditor assessment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average employees 50. Audit may also be triggered by group consolidation, public-interest status, or shareholder request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002) as transposition of EU Accounting Directive; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements and certain legal forms.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must file an annual confirmation of beneficial owners with the RBE in the month of the incorporation anniversary. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within 30 days of the event.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate statutory headline for a Luxembourg City SARL in FY2025 (17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax; reduced 15% CIT applies to the first EUR 200,000 taxable income under LIR art. 174).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Preferential regimes: (1) IP Box (LIR art. 50bis): 80% exemption of qualifying net IP income = effective 5% corporate tax on royalty streams; (2) Participation Exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains where a 10% holding is held for at least 12 months; (3) standard arm's-length cost deductibility for wholesale distribution expenses; (4) no notional interest deduction currently in force for commercial SOPARFI.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carry-forward for losses arising from tax year 2017 onward; pre-2017 losses are transitionally limited to 18 years; no carry-back mechanism in Luxembourg law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 700 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) with annexed Model 830 (impôt sur la fortune); electronic filing through the ACD eCDF portal via Guichet.lu / MyGuichet using a LuxTrust certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual-only statutory return; quarterly CIT prepayments (acomptes) are settled separately and do not constitute a filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year SARL, the Model 700 is due no later than 31 December of the year following the tax year; for split financial years, the administrative échéance is generally set within ten months after fiscal year-end unless a later formal extension is granted by the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A - Identification and tax unit details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, RCS number, address, legal form, tax ID (matricule), contact details, auditing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only if the SARL is a Luxembourg resident taxpayer; non-resident sellers without a PE do not file Model 700 but remain liable for Luxembourg-source WHT where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B - Accounting period and consolidation status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the financial year; fiscal consolidation or group regime flag.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the closing date matches the balance sheet date used for the audited accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross wholesale revenue from distribution of acetate and ophthalmic eyeglass frames, net of VAT, trade discounts, returns and rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident sells through a Luxembourg PE, allocate Luxembourg sourcing under the PE's books; otherwise show no Luxembourg turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C2 - Change in inventories and own work capitalised
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Variation of opening-to-closing stock of ophthalmic frames plus internally capitalised costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Luxembourg PE's warehouse stock movement is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commissions, agency overrides, FX gains, subsidies and other incidental operating revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Luxembourg-source ancillary income earned through the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases of frames and components, freight, royalties, personnel costs, occupancy, marketing, depreciation and amortisation, other business charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically borne by the Luxembourg PE are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income, interest income/costs, FX and derivative gains/losses, impairments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign dividend streams are reported with the applicable participation exemption claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income taxes and communal business tax, 50% of representation costs, excessive interest limitation disallowance, late-payment surcharges, and non-commercial gifts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same adjustment rules apply to PE results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E2 - Tax-exempt income and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, IP box deduction, investment tax credits and EU-source income relieving.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty and EU directive claims require a valid foreign TRC and 12-month holding evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section F - Tax loss carry-forward (reports en avant)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of prior-year losses against current taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry-forward applies only to losses suffered by the Luxembourg tax entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable base before application of CIT, solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final balance determines Luxembourg PE nexus and WHT computation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: formal mise en demeure; administrative fine of EUR 250 to EUR 2,500 per return; where no return is supplied, ACD assessment based on estimated profits plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.) on overdue CIT; intentional concealment triggers criminal tax fraud sanctions (up to EUR 250,000 fine and imprisonment).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax on SARL distributions to resident and non-resident shareholders (LIR art. 67); 0% applies where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions are met (10% holding, 12-month minimum, beneficiary ownership).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA or EU Directive relief: (1) obtain an annual, signature-dated Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's state issued for the distribution year; (2) file the official Luxembourg relief/refund application through MyGuichet or directly with the ACD service competent for the payer, using the standard form Modèle 72 for the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and the corresponding DTA-double taxation relief form for reduced treaty rates; (3) attach board minutes, share register extract evidencing a de jure and de facto 10% holding for at least 12 months, participation exemption certificate and economic substance documentation; (4) a beneficial-owner statement is mandatory. Advance tax ruling (décision anticipative) may proactively confirm the reduced/zero rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic Luxembourg WHT (no source taxation of recurring IP royalties paid by a Luxembourg SARL); statutory zero-rate remains available under all major Luxembourg DTAs. Interest: 0% domestic WHT for conventional bank and commercial debt interest paid cross-border; an exception applies to profit-participating or convertible bonds where the interest is recharacterised as a dividend, and to loans disallowed as sham debt, triggering the 15% dividend WHT; all payments remain subject to an arm's-length TP adjustment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory fixed EUR turnover threshold for Master File/Local File preparation in Luxembourg; in practice, an intercompany wholesale distributor such as the SARL must hold contemporaneous TP evidence on request by the ACD (typically within 30 days). Mandatory CbC notification and CbC Report apply where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000; a low-volume optical frames distributor will ordinarily only maintain a simplified Local File for intra-group purchases and financing above EUR 100,000 per transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a Cayman/UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but imposes OECD-aligned and ATAD-compliant substance requirements: the Participation Exemption, EU Parent-Subsidiary benefits, treaty relief and IP box advantages require the SARL to demonstrate physical premises, qualified staff, real wholesale distribution functions, commercial decision-making power, banking substance and an absence of artificial conduit arrangements; the ACD applies LIR art. 6 (abuse of law), the GAAR inherited from ATAD and circulaire LIR 264/1 when testing holding and finance structures. A letter-box distributor is exposed to re-characterisation of its profit allocation, denial of treaty/DTA benefits and reclassification of payments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Corporate Income Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally or recklessly filing a materially false Model 700 (undervaluation of wholesale turnover of acetate eyewear frames, fabricated supplier purchases, omission of financial income, overstatement of IP box deductions) or deliberate concealment of Luxembourg-source taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud sanction: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 250,000; administrative add-ons: penalty of 10% to 200% of the evaded CIT/municipal business tax, late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, and restitution of the shortfall; repeated or organised fraud increases penalties and triggers publication of the sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, gérants and de facto managers who signed false declarations or ordered the concealment are jointly and severally liable for the evaded taxes; aggravated cases lead to personal arrest warrants, travel and Schengen exit bans, disqualification from office and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell / Letterbox Company and GAAR Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an economically hollow SARL that registers in Luxembourg solely to channel invoice flows of high-value optical frames, holds no premises or personnel, lacks board substance, and passes profits onward without local decision-making or risk-bearing functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD recharacterisation of taxable profits into the beneficial owner's main jurisdiction; denial of DTA/EU Directive benefits and of the participation exemption; reclassification of financing or service payments as disguised dividends triggering the 15% WHT; administrative fine for non-filing and restitution of all undue refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be found personally liable for the re-assessed CIT and surcharges where the letter-box arrangement was used to defraud third parties or the state; civil restitution claims, travel bans and disqualification measures follow in bankruptcy or insolvency of the SARL.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Substance Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany sales, royalty or financing arrangements for ophthalmic eyewear frames departing from arm's-length prices; failure to deliver Master File/Local File or CbC report promptly; unjustified one-sided pricing to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative re-pricing by the ACD with an upward adjustment of the taxable base, denial of deductibility for the disallowed margin, interest of 0.6% per month; fines up to EUR 250,000 for CbC non-compliance in relevant groups; publication of adjustments; prolonged non-compliance may be escalated to tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certified transfer pricing documentation knowing it to be incomplete are jointly liable for the additional tax, withholding taxes and default interest; travel bans and imprisonment are available in cases of serious deliberate misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing large Swift/TT or platform payments without know-your-counterparty checks, invoicing sanctioned jurisdictions in the eyewear supply chain, deliberately obstructing the Luxembourg Registrar's beneficial-owner (UBO) register, or using pass-through transactions to launder distribution proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under the Law of 12 November 2004 as amended by the 2020 AML/CFT package: up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover for serious institutional breaches; individual criminal penalty of up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 250,000 fine for intentional money laundering; automatic freezing and confiscation of the object of the offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, civil confiscation orders, travel and banking prohibitions and accumulated director disqualification; knowing participation in a laundering scheme pierces the SARL's limitation of liability.
